questions.stem: What does one mitotic division produce?

options.text: Two cells with identical chromosome sets
options.explanation: Correct — this follows directly from the definition.
Four varied products belong to meiosis.
Division halves, it does not enlarge.
The diploid set is preserved.

questions.stem: What happens to chromosomes just before mitosis?

options.explanation: Gene swapping is not part of mitosis.
Correct — this matches the account taught above.
Shrinkage is not part of the sequence.
The chromosomes are the whole point.

questions.stem: During mitosis, what are the X-shaped structures seen in the cell?

options.explanation: Membranes do not form X shapes.
Nuclei re-form after the division.
Correct — this matches the account taught above.
The X shape is normal duplication, not mutation.

questions.stem: Why does each daughter cell end up diploid?

options.text: The cell borrows chromosomes from neighbours
options.explanation: Nothing is borrowed.
Duplication happens before the split.
Fertilisation is for gametes, not body cells.

options.text: Duplication before division keeps two copies of every chromosome in each new cell
options.explanation: Right — the other options each misplace a concept.

options.text: Duplicate, line up, pull apart, divide
options.explanation: Correct — this follows directly from the definition.
Halving and fusing belong elsewhere.
Duplication precedes division.
Fusing describes fertilisation.

questions.modelAnswer: Mitosis is nuclear division that gives rise to genetically identical cells.

questions.stem: List the uses of mitosis in the body.
questions.modelAnswer: Growth, repair of damaged tissue, replacement of cells, and asexual reproduction.

questions.stem: Explain why identical chromosome sets make mitosis suitable for repair.
questions.modelAnswer: Replacement tissue must match the original cells, and identical chromosome sets preserve that genetic identity, so the rebuilt tissue works like the tissue it replaces.

questions.stem: A lizard regrows its lost tail. State the division involved and what must be true of the new tail cells' chromosomes.
questions.modelAnswer: Mitosis rebuilds the tail, and the new cells must carry identical chromosome sets matching the original diploid cells.

questions.stem: Which cells of the body are not produced by mitosis from the zygote?

options.explanation: They derive from mitotic division during development.
Correct — this matches the account taught above.
Skin cells renew through mitosis.
Their precursors divide by mitosis.

questions.stem: What does asexual reproduction have in common with wound healing?

options.explanation: Neither requires gamete fusion.
Mitosis preserves the diploid set.

options.text: Both rely on mitosis to produce new cells
options.explanation: Yes — the mechanism works exactly this way.
Meiosis makes gametes, not new tissue or clones.

questions.stem: Why must red blood cells be replaced continually?

options.explanation: Wear and loss, not mutation, drive renewal.
Blood cells never become sex cells.
Replacement balances loss, not endless doubling.

options.text: They wear out, and mitosis supplies their replacements
options.explanation: Correct — this follows directly from the definition.

questions.stem: A zygote divides into an embryo. Which process is at work and why?

options.text: Mitosis, because the embryo needs identical copies for growth
options.explanation: Right — this is the account the lesson teaches.
Embryo building needs identity, not variation.

options.text: Fertilisation, because the egg must be fertilised again
options.explanation: Fertilisation already happened.
Change here comes from controlled division.

questions.stem: Which statement matches the taught account of cloning?

options.explanation: Asexual reproduction by mitosis needs none.

options.text: Mitosis produces offspring genetically identical to the parent
options.explanation: Correct — this matches the account taught above.
Mixing two parents is sexual reproduction.
Mitosis keeps the diploid set.

questions.stem: Name the four contexts in which mitosis occurs.
questions.modelAnswer: Growth, repair, cloning and asexual reproduction.

questions.stem: State the origin of all body cells apart from gametes.
questions.modelAnswer: They are produced by mitosis of the zygote.

questions.stem: Explain why a lost skin patch is restored with matching skin rather than a different tissue.
questions.modelAnswer: Mitosis copies the surrounding skin cells exactly, so the new cells carry the same chromosomes and mature into the same tissue type.

questions.stem: A gardener grows a whole strawberry plant from one cutting without any flowers or seeds. Name the reproduction type and the division that built the new roots and shoots.
questions.modelAnswer: It is asexual reproduction, and mitosis produced every new root and shoot cell, keeping the offspring genetically identical to the parent.
